In this assignment, you'll be picking up where you left off with the M&Ms activity. You'll load the data and perform some basic statistical analysis. Follow the steps below to complete the assignment.

### Task 1: Load the tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

### Task 2: Load the M&Ms dataset from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/mandms.csv
```{r}
mmdata <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/mandms.csv")
```


### Task 3: Sample 5 rows of data from the dataset

```{r}
set.seed(100)
sample_5 <- mmdata|> sample_n(5)
```


### Task 4: Calculate the mean age and standard deviation of the sample, using either the red or black number of M&Ms
```{r}
set.seed(100)
sample_5 <- mmdata|> sample_n(5)
mean(sample_5$red)
sd(sample_5$red)
```


### Task 5: Calculate the mean age and standard deviation of the population, using the same measure as in Task 4

```{r}
set.seed(100)
sample_5 <- mmdata|> sample_n(5)
mean(sample_5$total)
sd(sample_5$total)
```

### Task 6: Compare the sample and population statistics

Compare the two sets of means and standard deviations. Are they similar?

As I expected, the total population has a higher mean and SD then just the sample for red. I also checked for black and had similar results. I would not say they are wildly similar, however they are close to the numbers I was expecting. 

### Task 7: Describe the results

Write a few sentences about what you found in the data. What does this tell you about the M&Ms dataset and about the act of random sampling?

Based on what I found in the data for a sample of 5 rows from the dataset, the mean for the color red was 69.6 and the sd was 10.45466. For the same five rows, when you factor in the total (red + black), you yield a mean of 145.2 and an SD of 22.3. The act of random sampling can make your data look different depending on how you compare it. If I were to take a higher sample of rows, I would probably have much different results.
